thought.text: Permission issue: the `api` container runs as user `verein` (uid 1001) but the host `/workspace/api` tree is root-owned. Let me check and fix ownership:

reasoning_content:
There's a permission issue: the api container is running as user `verein` (uid 1001), but the host directory `/workspace/api` is owned by root. The mounted volume `./api:/var/www/html` is root-owned on the host, so the api container (user verein) can't write to storage/logs.

Also, the tooling container runs as user verein (uid 1001) and mounted `./:/var/www/html`. But `composer install` created `vendor/` owned by verein... and `php artisan` commands ran as verein. So files created by tooling are owned by uid 1001 (verein) on the host.

The api container is also running as verein (uid 1001) per the Dockerfile (adduser uid 1001). But wait, the error says permission denied on `/var/www/html/storage/logs/laravel.log`. The storage directory was created by the entrypoint running as verein... but maybe the existing `storage/` directory in the repo is root-owned, and `logs` subdirectory can't be created.

Let me check the permissions. The host `/workspace/api` is owned by root. The api container's entrypoint runs as verein (uid 1001) which is the same user as tooling. But the base directories are root-owned.

Actually, the issue is that the api container runs as `verein` (uid 1001), and the files in the repo (committed) are root-owned (uid 0) on the host. When tooling runs commands, they create new files as uid 1001, but pre-existing directories like `storage/logs` are root-owned.

Wait, but the tooling container also runs as verein (uid 1001) and it was able to run `php artisan key:generate` and `migrate:fresh` successfully — those write to `.env` (which was created fresh, so verein can write it) and to the database. But `filament:assets` wrote to `public/` successfully.

The problem now is the api container trying to write to `storage/logs/laravel.log`. Let me check ownership of the storage directory.

Actually the cleanest fix: chown the api directory to uid 1001:1001 so the verein user in the api container can write to it. Let me check the current state.

action.command: ls -la /workspace/api/storage/ 2>&1; echo '--- logs ---'; ls -la /workspace/api/storage/logs/ 2>&1; echo '--- api dir owner ---'; ls -ld /workspace/api /workspace/api/storage/framework 2>&1

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "ls -la /workspace/api/storage/ 2>&1; echo '--- logs ---'; ls -la /workspace/api/storage/logs/ 2>&1; echo '--- api dir owner ---'; ls -ld /workspace/api /workspace/api/storage/framework 2>&1", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Check storage dir ownership"}
